topicTitle: Punjab Crisis & Accord, Kashmir Situation, Assam Accord, North-East Sub-nationalisms

sections: 1. Region and the Nation (Indian approach to diversity)
2. Jammu and Kashmir (Roots of conflict, Article 370, Sheikh Abdullah, 1989 insurgency)
3. Punjab (Anandpur Sahib Resolution 1973, Operation Blue Star 1984, Rajiv-Longowal Accord 1985)
4. The North-East (Autonomy demands, Secessionist movements in Mizoram & Nagaland, Assam Accord 1985)

summary30s: The Indian approach balances regional aspirations with national unity, treating regional identities as legitimate democratic expressions rather than anti-national threats.
In Punjab, the Anandpur Sahib Resolution (1973) sought federal autonomy; militancy led to Operation Blue Star (June 1984), Indira Gandhi's assassination, and the Rajiv-Longowal Accord (1985).
Kashmir experienced deep political turbulence under Article 370, culminating in an eruption of armed cross-border militancy in 1989.
The Assam Movement (1979-85) led by AASU against illegal migrants produced the 15 August 1985 Assam Accord (24 March 1971 deportation cutoff date).
In the North-East, two decades of insurgency in Mizoram ended with the historic Mizo Peace Accord (1986) between Rajiv Gandhi and MNF leader Laldenga.

coreConcepts.title: The Punjab Crisis: Anandpur Sahib Resolution to Operation Blue Star
coreConcepts.explanation: In 1973, the Shiromani Akali Dal passed the 'Anandpur Sahib Resolution' asserting regional autonomy, redrawing Centre-State relations, and recognizing the distinct identity of Sikhs. In the 1980s, the movement was hijacked by armed extremists led by Jarnail Singh Bhindranwale, who fortified the Golden Temple complex in Amritsar. In June 1984, the Government of India launched 'Operation Blue Star'—a military operation using tanks and commandos to flush out militants. The temple was damaged, deeply hurting Sikh sentiments. On 31 October 1984, Prime Minister Indira Gandhi was assassinated by two of her Sikh bodyguards at her residence. In the aftermath, horrific anti-Sikh violence erupted in Delhi and North India, killing over 2,000 Sikhs. In July 1985, Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi signed the Punjab Accord with moderate Akali leader Harchand Singh Longowal (transfer of Chandigarh to Punjab, water-sharing commissions). Longowal was assassinated by extremists weeks later.
coreConcepts.ncertPointer: Politics in India Since Independence, Chapter 8, Section 3
coreConcepts.examTip: Anandpur Sahib Resolution = 1973; Operation Blue Star = June 1984; Rajiv-Longowal Punjab Accord = July 1985.

coreConcepts.title: Jammu and Kashmir: Autonomy, Accord, and 1989 Insurgency
coreConcepts.explanation: Article 370 granted Jammu and Kashmir special constitutional autonomy (own state constitution, union jurisdiction limited). In 1953, Prime Minister Sheikh Abdullah was dismissed and detained for advocating plebiscite. In 1975, Indira Gandhi and Sheikh Abdullah signed the 'Indira-Sheikh Accord', whereby Abdullah accepted Jammu and Kashmir's accession as permanent and became Chief Minister. In 1987, assembly elections were widely perceived as rigged by the National Conference-Congress coalition, creating deep disillusionment among Kashmiri youth. In 1989, a full-scale armed separatist insurgency erupted, aided by training and weapons from Pakistan, leading to mass violence and the tragic exodus of Kashmiri Pandits from the Valley.
coreConcepts.ncertPointer: Politics in India Since Independence, Chapter 8, Section 2
coreConcepts.examTip: 1975 Indira-Sheikh Accord: Sheikh Abdullah became CM of J&K, accepting the accession as final.

coreConcepts.title: The Assam Movement and the 1985 Assam Accord
coreConcepts.explanation: In 1979, the All Assam Students Union (AASU) and Asom Gana Sangram Parishad launched a massive anti-foreigner movement against undocumented migrants from Bangladesh, fearing indigenous Assamese would be reduced to a minority in their homeland. The 6-year agitation was marked by strikes, economic blockades, and communal violence (Nellie massacre, 1983). On 15 August 1985, Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi signed the historic 'Assam Accord' with AASU leaders (Prafulla Kumar Mahanta). Key terms: (1) All foreigners who entered Assam between 1 January 1966 and 24 March 1971 would be detected, disenfranchised for 10 years, and regularized thereafter; (2) All migrants entering on or after 25 March 1971 would be detected and deported. AASU transformed into the Asom Gana Parishad (AGP) and won the December 1985 assembly elections.
coreConcepts.ncertPointer: Politics in India Since Independence, Chapter 8, Section 4
coreConcepts.examTip: Assam Accord cutoff dates: 1 Jan 1966 to 24 March 1971 (disenfranchised 10 yrs); 25 March 1971 onwards (expulsion/deportation).

coreConcepts.title: North-East Peace Accords: Mizoram and Nagaland
coreConcepts.explanation: Following a devastating bamboo famine ('Mautam') in 1959, the Assam government's apathy led Laldenga to form the Mizo National Front (MNF). In 1966, MNF launched an armed rebellion declaring independence; the Indian Air Force carried out air strikes in Aizawl. After two decades of guerrilla warfare, a peaceful breakthrough occurred: on 30 June 1986, the 'Mizo Peace Accord' was signed between Rajiv Gandhi and Laldenga. Full statehood was granted to Mizoram, MNF gave up arms, and Laldenga became Chief Minister, making Mizoram one of the most peaceful states in India. In Nagaland, the Naga National Council (NNC) under Angami Zapu Phizo demanded sovereign independence from 1951, leading to armed conflict; later, a faction signed the Shillong Accord in 1975, while the NSCN continued guerrilla resistance.
coreConcepts.ncertPointer: Politics in India Since Independence, Chapter 8, Section 4
coreConcepts.examTip: Mizo Peace Accord signed in 1986 with Laldenga, transforming a violent insurgency into a peaceful democratic state.

workedExamples.question:
Under the historic Assam Accord signed on 15 August 1985, what was the cutoff date for detecting and deporting foreigners who entered Assam without authorization?
(A) 26 January 1950
(B) 1 January 1966
(C) 25 March 1971
(D) 15 August 1985
workedExamples.explanation: According to the Assam Accord, those who entered Assam on or after 25 March 1971 were to be identified and expelled/deported. Those who arrived between 1 January 1966 and 24 March 1971 were disenfranchised for 10 years.
solutionStepByStep: Step 1: Check the two cutoff dates in the Assam Accord.
Step 2: 1 Jan 1966 - 24 March 1971 -> disenfranchised for 10 years.
Step 3: 25 March 1971 onwards -> targeted for immediate detection and deportation.
workedExamples.cuetPattern: Precise date identification in landmark modern peace accords.
solutionSteps: Step 1: Check the two cutoff dates in the Assam Accord.
Step 2: 1 Jan 1966 - 24 March 1971 -> disenfranchised for 10 years.

workedExamples.question:
Who was the leader of the Mizo National Front (MNF) who led an armed rebellion from 1966 and eventually signed the Mizo Peace Accord in 1986, becoming Chief Minister?
(A) Angami Zapu Phizo
(B) Laldenga
(C) Prafulla Kumar Mahanta
(D) Harchand Singh Longowal
workedExamples.explanation: Laldenga formed the Mizo National Front in 1959 following the Mautam famine. In 1986, he signed the peace accord with Rajiv Gandhi, ending two decades of insurgency, and became Chief Minister of Mizoram.
solutionStepByStep: Step 1: Phizo was the leader of Naga National Council (NNC).
Step 2: Laldenga was the leader of Mizo National Front (MNF).
Step 3: Mahanta was AASU leader in Assam; Longowal was Akali leader in Punjab.
solutionSteps: Step 1: Phizo was the leader of Naga National Council (NNC).

commonTraps.correctConcept: Angami Zapu Phizo was the leader of NAGALAND (Naga National Council); Laldenga was the leader of MIZORAM (Mizo National Front).
commonTraps.whyTrapWorks: Both were North-Eastern insurgent leaders who fought for independence in the 1950s-60s.

commonTraps.misconception: Believing the Assam Accord expelled all migrants who entered Assam after 1951.
commonTraps.correctConcept: AASU initially demanded 1951 as the base year, but the compromise signed in 1985 set 25 March 1971 (the day Bangladesh Liberation War began) as the cutoff for expulsion.
commonTraps.whyTrapWorks: Questions ask whether 1951 or 1971 was agreed as the cutoff date.
commonTraps.cuetWarning: Deportation cutoff date agreed in Assam Accord = 25 March 1971.

practiceQuestions.question: In which year did the Indian Army carry out 'Operation Blue Star' to clear armed militants from the Golden Temple in Amritsar?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Operation Blue Star was conducted in June 1984 by the Indian Army in the Golden Temple.

practiceQuestions.question: The Punjab Accord of July 1985 was signed between Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi and which moderate Akali leader?
practiceQuestions.explanation: In July 1985, Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi reached an agreement with Harchand Singh Longowal, then President of the Shiromani Akali Dal.

practiceQuestions.question: Which student organization led the six-year anti-foreigner movement in Assam between 1979 and 1985?
practiceQuestions.explanation: The All Assam Students Union (AASU) was an anti-foreigner student movement that led the agitation starting in 1979.

practiceQuestions.question: In which year was the historic Mizo Peace Accord signed between Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi and MNF leader Laldenga?
practiceQuestions.explanation: In 1986, a peace agreement was signed between Rajiv Gandhi and Laldenga, granting Mizoram full statehood.

practiceQuestions.question: What natural calamity in 1959 triggered deep resentment in the Mizo Hills against the Assam state government, leading to the formation of the Mizo National Front?

options.text: The Mautam famine caused by bamboo flowering and rat population boom

practiceQuestions.explanation: The Mautam famine occurred in 1959 when bamboo flowered and rats multiplied, destroying crops. Inadequate relief led to the formation of the MNF.

practiceQuestions.question: Under the 1975 Indira-Sheikh Accord, who became the Chief Minister of Jammu and Kashmir after more than two decades of political isolation?
practiceQuestions.explanation: In 1975, Indira Gandhi signed an accord with Sheikh Abdullah, who became the Chief Minister of Jammu and Kashmir.

practiceQuestions.question: Who was the legendary leader of the Naga National Council (NNC) who declared Nagaland's independence in 1951 and led guerrilla warfare?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Angami Zapu Phizo led a section of the Nagas in an armed struggle for sovereign independence starting in the 1950s.

practiceQuestions.question: What political party was formed by the leaders of the All Assam Students Union (AASU) following the signing of the Assam Accord in 1985?
practiceQuestions.explanation: AASU and Asom Gana Sangram Parishad organized themselves as a regional political party called Asom Gana Parishad (AGP) in 1985.

practiceQuestions.question: In which year did the Shiromani Akali Dal pass the famous 'Anandpur Sahib Resolution' articulating demands for greater regional and federal autonomy?
practiceQuestions.explanation: The Anandpur Sahib Resolution was passed at a conference of the Akali Dal in 1973.

practiceQuestions.question:
Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): The democratic settlement of the Mizo crisis through the 1986 Accord is celebrated as one of the most successful conflict resolution triumphs in independent India.
Reason (R): The Accord integrated insurgent leaders into the democratic constitutional process, granting Mizoram full statehood and transforming a two-decade armed struggle into lasting peace.

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)

practiceQuestions.explanation: The Mizo Accord successfully ended twenty years of insurgency by accommodating regional autonomy within the constitutional framework. Both are true and (R) explains (A).
